{{Short description|Geometric operation}}

A '''Procrustes transformation''' is a geometric transformation that involves only [[translation (geometry)|translation]], [[rotation]], [[uniform scaling]], or a [[Function composition|combination]] of these [[Linear transformation|transformations]]. Hence, it may change the size, position, and orientation  of a geometric object, but not its [[shape]].

The Procrustes transformation is named after the mythical Greek robber [[Procrustes]]<ref name="Ramsay2007">{{cite book |last1=Ramsay |first1=J. O. |last2=Silverman |first2=B. W. |title=Applied Functional Data Analysis: Methods and Case Studies |date=23 November 2007 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0-387-22465-7 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WE3SzeVEvDkC&pg=PA61 |access-date=1 November 2024 |language=en}}</ref> who made his victims fit his bed either by stretching their limbs or cutting them off.
